info.title: HR Platform API
info.description: Internal HR management platform — auth, employees, leaves, standups, projects, servers, payroll, profile, reports, and integrations (Google Calendar, Discord, generic webhooks).

tags.name: Goals
tags.description: Individual, team, and company goals / KPI tracking

tags.name: Feedback
tags.description: Peer, manager, and public recognition feedback notes

tags.name: Google Calendar
tags.description: Google OAuth connection and calendar sync

tags.name: Meetings
tags.description: Scheduled meetings backed by Google Calendar

tags.name: Discord
tags.description: Discord bot / Webhook Events integration for standups

tags.name: Email Settings

tags.name: Onboard
tags.description: Public onboarding applications and contract review

bearerAuth.description: Obtained from POST /api/auth/login. Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

status.description: Create only — 'onboarding' creates a pending applicant (is_active = false) awaiting approval via PUT /{id}/approve or PUT /{id}/reject.

discord_username.description: Update only — matched against Discord standup submissions

ip_address.description: Masked as •••••••• when is_sensitive=true and show_sensitive is not requested

ssh_user.description: Masked as •••••••• when is_sensitive=true and show_sensitive is not requested

email.description: Must be on an allowed organization domain

current_password.description: Required if the account already has a password set

token.description: Token from the reset-password email link

effective_rate.description: Estimated effective tax rate as a percentage

smtp_pass.description: Required on initial setup; omit to keep the stored password unchanged

password.description: Left unchanged if omitted/blank on update

nda_path.description: Stored filename of the uploaded signed contract

get.description: Use this endpoint to verify that the server is up and running. The response will include the server's status and the current timestamp.

post.description: Logs in a user by providing their email and password. Validates email domain and returns a JWT for 7 days. Returns appropriate errors for missing credentials or invalid domain.

put.description: This endpoint allows a logged-in user to change their password. Provide a valid JSON object with the new password details in the request body to update the password.

post.description: Sends a generic message to request a password reset, regardless of the email's existence to avoid enumeration attacks.
Use this endpoint to reset your password by providing a valid reset token sent via email and a new password. Ensure the token is valid and not expired to proceed with the password reset process.

get.summary: Get aggregated headcount, leave, and project stats
get.description: This endpoint provides aggregated data on employee headcount, leave balances, and project status. It's secured with Bearer token authentication. The response is in JSON format, containing the aggregated stats as described in the DashboardStats schema.
This endpoint provides an array of daily counts for standup submissions over the last 30 days. It is secured with bearer authentication, and the response is a JSON array of TrendPoint objects.
This endpoint provides an array of daily counts for leave request submissions over the last 30 days. It can be used by frontend engineers to visualize leave request trends on a dashboard.
This API endpoint allows you to fetch a list of all active employees. It returns an array of employee objects in JSON format.

post.description: Create a new employee record, including default leave balances for the current year. This operation is used to add a new employee to the system.

get.description: Returns a list of employees marked for onboarding (is_active = false). Use only with Admin permissions.
This endpoint retrieves details of an employee identified by a unique ID. Provide the ID in the URL to fetch the employee's information.

put.description: This endpoint allows updating the details of an employee by providing their unique ID and the updated fields in the request body.

delete.description: This operation soft-deletes an employee by setting their 'is_active' field to false. It accepts an employee ID in the path parameter to identify the employee to be deactivated.

get.description: Fetch detailed payroll information for a specific employee, including their working days, leave days, and expected pay based on their current salary. This API is useful for HR systems to provide real-time payroll insights.

put.description: This API endpoint is used to approve an employee who is in the 'onboarding' status. It sets the 'is_active' field to true and updates the 'status' to 'active', along with sending a one-time password to the employee's company email. Only Admins can use this endpoint.

400.description: Employee is not a pending applicant

put.description: Ends the onboarding process for an employee by deleting their record. Use this API only for employees in the 'onboarding' status.

parameters.name: send_mail
parameters.description: If true, sends a rejection notice to the employee before deleting their record.

400.description: Employee is not a pending applicant

get.description: This endpoint allows users to retrieve a list of leave requests. Employees can filter by their own ID, and admins/leads can further filter by status and employee ID.

to.description: If provided, sends a notification email via the employee's configured SMTP settings

post.description: This API allows submitting a leave request for an employee. It requires the employee's ID, leave type, start and end dates, and optionally the reason for the leave and notification details.

put.description: Use this endpoint to update a pending leave request by its ID. Ensure the request comes from the authorized employee and the leave status is 'pending'.

delete.description: This API endpoint allows the cancellation of a pending leave request. It requires the employee ID in the path parameter and can be called by the owning employee to cancel the leave if the status is still 'pending'.

get.description: This endpoint returns an array of objects representing employees who are approved for leave today. Each object includes the employee's name, designation, profile picture URL (optional), leave type, and end date of leave.

get.summary: Get employees on leave this week

200.description: Array of employees out this week

get.description: This endpoint retrieves a list of employees who are currently on approved leave that falls within the week spanning Monday through Friday. The response is an array of objects, each containing details such as the employee's name, designation, leave type, start date, and end date.
This API call retrieves the current year's leave balances for a specified employee ID. The response is an array of objects, each representing a leave type and its balance.

put.description: Approves a leave request by an admin or lead. The request includes a 'reviewed_by' field indicating the approver. This action deducts leave days from the employee's balance and checks if the leave dates have passed.
Admins can reject leave requests by their subordinates, ensuring requests are processed within the required timeframe. Users must provide a reviewer's ID to validate the rejection.

get.description: Employees can filter standups by exact date, while admins/leads can see all standups and filter by employee ID or date range.

post.description: This API allows you to submit a daily standup report for a specific employee. It supports submitting data in JSON format, including details like yesterday's and today's work, blockers, and the date. The standup report is saved and, if configured, mirrored to a Discord channel.

get.summary: Today's own standups or admin/lead access required
get.description: Get an array of standups submitted today. Access is limited to the user's own entries unless the user has admin or lead privileges. Use this endpoint to retrieve standup submissions for today.
This endpoint retrieves an array of projects an employee is assigned to, including their role and milestones. It requires the employee's unique ID as a path parameter.
This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of all projects, with optional filtering by their status (active, archived, on_hold).

post.description: This endpoint allows you to create a new project with optional parameters such as name, description, repositories, documentation URLs, status, start date, and expected end date.

put.description: Use this endpoint to modify an existing project by providing updated project details in the request body. Ensure the project ID is correctly specified in the path to avoid conflicts with other projects.

get.description: Use this endpoint to retrieve a list of team assignments associated with a specific project ID. Ensure you pass the project ID in the URL to fetch the correct assignments.

post.description: Assigns a specific employee to a project identified by ID, allowing you to update their role within the project.

delete.description: This endpoint allows removing an employee from a specific project by specifying the project ID and the employee ID in the URL. It responds with a 200 status code upon successful removal.

get.description: This endpoint retrieves a list of milestones associated with a specific project identified by the provided ID. It is useful for frontend developers who need to fetch and display project milestones on their web or mobile applications.

post.description: Use this endpoint to add a new milestone to a specific project. The request body should include the milestone's title, due date, and status.

put.description: This operation allows updating the title, due date, and status of a specific milestone within a project. The status must be one of 'pending', 'in_progress', or 'completed'.

get.description: This API endpoint allows fetching a list of service keys linked to a specific project identified by its ID. It's useful for developers who need to retrieve the service keys associated with a project for further processing or display.

post.summary: Link service to project by ID
post.description: This endpoint allows you to associate a service with a project by providing the project ID and the service key in the request body. It's an idempotent operation, meaning you can make the call multiple times with the same parameters and it will have the same effect.

delete.description: This operation removes a service from a specified project, allowing you to unlink a service from a project by providing the project ID and service key in the request.

get.description: This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of servers associated with a specific project_id. You can also specify the show_sensitive parameter to reveal sensitive fields, which is only accessible to users with the lead/admin role.

post.description: Use this endpoint to create a new server registration. Provide the server's name, environment, IP address, domain, SSH user, and any notes or sensitive information. The endpoint will return a successful status upon successful registration.

put.description: This API endpoint allows updating server details by providing the server's ID and the updated server information in JSON format. The response is a 200 status code with a success schema if the update is successful.

delete.description: This API endpoint allows you to delete a server record by specifying its ID in the request URL. It returns a 200 status code upon successful deletion.

get.description: This endpoint provides a list of the latest 50 culture events. Developers can use this to fetch and display the most recent cultural activities on their applications.

post.description: To create a new event, you need to provide the title, event type, and event date in the request body. The event type can be 'birthday', 'anniversary', 'team_event', or 'milestone'. If you want to associate the event with an employee, you can include their ID. The response will be a success message with a status code of 201.

get.description: This endpoint provides an array of upcoming events that occur within the next 30 days. It can be used by frontend engineers to display or filter events in real-time.
Returns an array of payroll records for employees. The records are accessible based on the user's role: Admins/leads can see all active employees, others only their own record.

put.description: This API allows updating an employee's salary and pay frequency. Use it only when you have the appropriate permissions.
This endpoint allows an admin to reset the password for a specific employee. The admin must provide the employee's ID and a new password to update.

get.description: Returns an array of tax profiles for employees, with estimated tax based on Nepal's tax slabs, suitable for admins and leads to view all records, while others can only see their own.

put.description: Use this API to update an employee's tax profile information. Developers should ensure the API call is made with the correct employee ID and include the necessary tax profile details in the request body.

get.description: Retrieve a list of goals for a specific employee, with optional status and category filters.

post.description: Creates a new goal for the authenticated user. Admins and leads can assign goals to others.

get.summary: Get aggregated goal completions per employee
get.description: This endpoint returns an array of goal completion summaries for each employee, useful for frontend developers needing to display or integrate aggregated goal data.

put.description: This API endpoint allows updating the details of a goal by providing the goal's ID and the updated goal details in JSON format. Only owners or administrators with appropriate permissions can update goals.

delete.description: Use this endpoint to remove a goal by its ID. Ensure you have the necessary permissions or are an authorized admin/lead to perform this action.

put.description: This API endpoint allows updating the progress value and status of a specific goal. It requires a goal ID and a JSON payload containing the new progress value and status. Only users with appropriate permissions can update the goal progress.

get.description: This endpoint allows users to retrieve a list of performance reviews. Employees can see their own reviews, while admins/leads can view all reviews and filter by employee_id. Status filters are available for draft, submitted, and acknowledged reviews.

post.description: Create a draft performance review for an employee. Only administrators and leads with the appropriate permissions can use this endpoint.

400.description: A review for this period already exists

get.description: This endpoint retrieves the rating history for a specific employee, including their scores across various review periods. It requires the employee's ID to fetch the relevant data.

put.description: This endpoint allows updating a performance review draft. It's intended for administrators or leads who have the appropriate permissions and only when the review's status is 'draft'.

400.description: Only draft reviews can be edited

delete.description: Deletes a draft review for performance evaluations. Only available for admin or lead users when the review status is 'draft'. The request should be made using DELETE method to the /api/performance/{id} endpoint.

400.description: Only draft reviews can be deleted

put.description: Submits a previously drafted review to an employee. This endpoint is intended for administrative or lead users to submit reviews that have been prepared beforehand.
Acknowledges a submitted performance review by the employee who submitted it. Only the reviewed employee can acknowledge the review while its status is 'submitted'.

400.description: Only submitted reviews can be acknowledged

get.description: Retrieve a list of feedback notes based on scope and type, useful for companies or individual users to view their own or others' feedback.

400.description: Missing message or sending feedback to yourself

post.description: This operation allows users to send a feedback note to another employee. Users must provide a feedback message in the request body, which includes the message content. The request requires a valid JSON payload for successful execution.

get.description: This endpoint provides a list of feedback counts per employee. It is useful for a frontend engineer who needs to display or analyze the number of feedbacks received by each employee, typically for a leaderboard or dashboard display.

delete.description: This API allows authorized users to delete a feedback note identified by its unique ID. Ensure you have the appropriate permissions to delete the feedback.

get.description: Use this endpoint to retrieve the profile information of the currently logged-in employee. Ensure your API call includes the necessary authentication (Bearer token) as part of the request headers.

put.description: This API allows you to update the editable fields of your profile. The request body should include the fields you wish to update.

post.description: This API allows you to upload or replace your profile photo. It accepts image files in .jpg, .jpeg, .png, or .webp formats, with a maximum size of 5 MB. The API deletes the previous photo if a new one is provided.

This endpoint allows you to upload a front or back citizenship document image. It supports .jpg, .jpeg, .png, and .webp files up to 5 MB. The previous file for the specified side will be deleted. The request requires a multipart/form-data body with a 'doc' field containing the image.

400.description: Invalid side or no file uploaded

get.description: Returns an array of monthly reports filtered by year and month, suitable for frontend developers to integrate into their applications.

post.description: This API endpoint allows you to submit a monthly report file for processing. It supports .pdf, .pptx, .ppt, .docx, and .doc files up to 20 MB in size. The request body requires the file, employee_id, title, month, and year fields, along with optional notes.

400.description: Missing required fields or no file

get.description: Allows non-privileged users to download their own report files, provided the report exists and the user has permission to access it.

delete.description: This endpoint allows a user to delete their own report. It requires authentication and deletes both the report from the system and the associated file.

get.description: This endpoint returns the URL needed for users to authenticate with Google OAuth. It is intended for use by administrators only.

get.summary: Exchange auth code for tokens and redirect to frontend calendar page
get.description: This endpoint receives an auth code from Google in the query parameters, exchanges it for tokens, stores the tokens, and then redirects the frontend to the calendar page using the FRONTEND_URL/calendar endpoint.

302.description: Redirect to FRONTEND_URL/calendar with a status query param

get.description: This API endpoint returns the connection status of the user's Google Calendar. It is secured with Bearer token and returns a JSON object detailing the status.

delete.description: Stops push notifications and clears tokens. Use only with admin credentials.

post.description: This endpoint allows users to manually sync their upcoming Google Calendar events into scheduled meetings. Developers can integrate this endpoint to automatically sync calendar events, ensuring meeting schedules are up-to-date with event information from Google Calendar.
Called by Google to notify changes in your Calendar. Use the x-goog-resource-state header to indicate state changes, then respond with 200 OK to acknowledge.

get.description: This endpoint retrieves a list of scheduled meetings from the last 7 days. It is secured using bearer authentication, and the response is an array of meeting objects.

post.summary: Create Google Meeting and Calendar Event
post.description: This endpoint allows you to create a new meeting, which also sets up a matching event in Google Calendar. You need to provide the necessary details in the request body, which includes fields like meeting name, start time, end time, and participants. Upon successful creation, a matching calendar event is created with a link for the meeting.

delete.description: This endpoint cancels a meeting by its ID. Only the creator or an admin can perform this action, which soft-deletes the meeting by setting its status to 'cancelled'.

post.description: Handles the /standup command and validates signatures for secure interactions. Use the provided headers for authentication and include the interaction payload in the request body.

200.description: Interaction response (PING ack or slash-command reply)

post.description: This endpoint allows submitting a standup record for a Discord channel. It requires a valid X-Internal-Token header for authentication and includes fields for the standup details.

get.description: This endpoint retrieves the SMTP settings for a specific employee without exposing their stored password.

put.summary: Create or update SMTP settings for an employee
put.description: smtp_pass is required on first save; omit it on later updates to keep the existing password. Test-verifies the SMTP connection asynchronously when a password is provided.

get.description: This endpoint allows retrieval of stored service credentials associated with a specific employee identified by the employeeId. The response is an array of credentials, which can be used to authenticate and access protected services securely.

post.summary: Create or update service credential for employee
post.description: This API allows you to create or update a service credential for a specific employee. The employee's ID is provided in the URL path. You can include a service name and password in the request body to modify or add a credential.

get.description: This endpoint verifies a webhook challenge sent by the sender. It echoes back the provided 'hub.challenge' value as plain text, ensuring the webhook is correctly configured and authenticating the sender's identity using the 'hub.verify_token'.

200.description: Challenge echoed back as plain text

post.description: This endpoint allows receiving a payload sent from an external service. It handles Slack-style verification requests and always responds with a 200 OK immediately, with the actual processing happening asynchronously.

schema.description: Arbitrary event payload, or a Slack url_verification challenge

200.description: Acknowledged (or challenge echoed for Slack verification)

get.description: This endpoint allows you to fetch a month-end report from the system. It's useful for integrating with n8n workflows where you need to process monthly data.

200.description: sucessfully send data to n8n webhook

503.description: Error in sending request to n8n workflow

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Which onboarding form layout to fetch

get.description: This endpoint retrieves the form layout for either intern or employee onboarding. You can specify the type of form layout you need through the 'type' query parameter.

post.description: This endpoint allows setting the layout for onboarding forms. Admin/lead users can use this to update the form layout.

get.description: This endpoint lists onboarding profiles based on the specified type. You can request all profiles, intern profiles, or employee profiles by including the type query parameter in your request.

post.description: Use this endpoint to submit an onboarding application with a signed contract. The request includes a JSON-formatted payload and a binary file for the contract in a multipart form data format.

patch.description: This operation allows approved administrators to approve an existing onboarding profile by its ID, ensuring the process is handled securely with appropriate permissions.

delete.description: This endpoint allows administrators or leads to remove a specific onboarding profile. It requires the 'bearerAuth' security and accepts a required 'id' parameter in the path to identify the profile to be deleted.

get.description: This API endpoint allows you to view the uploaded contract file associated with a specific onboarding profile by its ID. The response will be a stream of the PDF file in application/pdf format.
